note_en: Verb + 得 + description tells you how far an action goes: 锅要烧得极热 "the wok must be heated until it's extremely hot," and later 锅烧得够热 "the wok was hot enough." English might say "heat the wok red-hot," putting the result straight after the verb, but Chinese needs 得 to link the action to its degree. The same pattern shows up in 正看得入神 "I was watching, completely absorbed."
